graph partitioning algorithms decrease communication substantially (by up to 99%) and that processing RDF triples as single triples rather than graph fragments increases throughput.
graph partitioning based workload scheduling in distributed stream processing systems can decrease inter machine traffic substantially (by up to 99%) whilst maintaining an even load distribution.

graph partitioning based scheduling can reduce communication overhead substantially, that semantics may increase throughput, and that the use of graph partitioning may even increase scalability of distributed systems.

the problem of scheduling distributed workload in a network aware manner.
the question of how the data and computation load can be partitioned and scheduled within distributed stream processing systems to minimize network load and to maximize throughput.
the question how to schedule distributed stream processing workloads to minimize network load whilst ensuring a balanced workload distribution.

a uniform distribution strategy is not necessarily the best choice for all scenarios and that the use of a graph based partitioning strategy is a good starting point.

the proposed graph partitioning based scheduling approach is a promising alternative to the uniform scheduling strategy and that the semantics of the data can have a significant impact on the performance of distributed stream processing engines.

network aware workload scheduling is essential for distributed stream processing systems to achieve high throughput.
